text: Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code cleaner and easier to understand, not to add new features. For example, you might break a long, complicated function into smaller, simpler ones, or rename variables so they clearly describe their purpose. This reduces technical debt, which is the extra work created by messy code that is hard to maintain. While refactoring takes time, it greatly improves readability for you and your team. In the long run, it saves hours of confusion and makes future changes much faster and safer.
